review_notes.first_candidate_rejected: Candidate 435f233 was rejected by an independent reviewer who compiled a probe against the candidate's own source and proved four real leaks while the acceptance still exited 0: a quoted value in JSON, an Authorization header inside single-line JSON, the body of a PEM private key, and credentials in URL userinfo. The cause was that the sealed vectors had been shaped around the author's own regular expressions.
review_notes.sensitivity_proof: Reverting only internal/security/redaction/redaction.go to the rejected version makes the acceptance exit 1 with AUR-009/AC-001/behavior-missing, so the six added vectors are load bearing rather than decorative. Four of them deliberately carry a non-canary secret, because with the canary present the registered-secret layer would rescue the output and the vector would be born green.
review_notes.mutations: MUT-001 and MUT-002 each exit 1 with their declared code, and both restores return byte-identical observation digests.
review_notes.reviewer_attacks: Over twenty further vectors were attempted against the candidate source - unicode-escaped values, obs-fold headers, single quotes with spaces, percent-encoded userinfo with a port, CRLF and malformed PEM banners, and a canary split across three writes - and none leaked the canary. The typed limit error carries zero bytes and zero effects.
review_notes.open_findings: Four findings remain, none of them a canary leak and none producing a false green: docs/specs/AUR-009.md promises generic scheme://user@host userinfo while the expression enumerates only https, http, wss, ws, ftp, ssh and git, so postgres:// passes intact; the auth-header rules are still anchored at line start, so a header mid-line is only saved by the registered-secret rule; the double-quoted JSON rules stop at an escaped quote; and material on the same line as a PEM BEGIN banner survives. They belong to a follow-up card against the filter, not to this delivery.
